why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier's probes. Builder step 2 gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042'; padLeft('42', 5) === '   42'". Verifier Check 1 tests these same calls, p('42',5,'0') and p('42',5), and expects the same results, "00042" and "   42". Step 4 repeats "('42', 5, '0' -> '00042')" as a test case to write. So the builder brief contains inputs with expected outputs that are also in the verifier brief. The builder's other example, ('12345',3,'0'), isn't a verifier input, but the two shared pairs are enough to break the criterion. Running npm test and writing its own tests are allowed, but these shared probe pairs are not.
